sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
1. Add a `GET /healthz` endpoint that returns `{"status":"ok"}` and a `GET /readyz` that pings the model with a trivial prompt (1 token) and returns 503 if it fails. Wire both into your load balancer.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>
Use a tiny Pydantic AI agent or `llm.ainvoke("ping")` inside `asyncio.wait_for`. Health checks should never call the model — readiness checks should.
</details>

2. Replace the in-memory `hits` dict with a Redis-backed limiter using `INCR` + `EXPIRE`. Test by running two uvicorn workers (`--workers 2`) and confirming the limit is shared.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>
Key format: `ratelimit:{ip}:{int(time.time() // 60)}`. `INCR` returns the count; if it is `1`, also `EXPIRE` the key for the window length.
</details>

3. Add OpenTelemetry tracing to Project 2 so each LCEL chain step appears as a child span. Export to a local Jaeger container.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>
Use `opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi` for the framework and a custom `RunnableLambda` wrapper that opens a span per step. LangChain has experimental `LangChainTracer` for the latter.
</details>
